audit_scope.description: This batch covers both EL components (EVM memory operations, precompile dispatch, block header validation, receipt encoding, elliptic curve precompiles, EIP-712 box types) and CL components (beacon chain payload processing with block access lists, light client P2P networking, deposit tree snapshots, validator withdrawals, testnet reset lifecycle).

in_scope: EVM Memory Operations (MLOAD, MSTORE, MSTORE8, MCOPY)
Execution Payload Processing (EIP-7928 Block Access Lists)
Light Client P2P Gossip and Req/Resp

misclassified_entities.reason: Internal EVM component. Smart contracts calling precompiles execute within the EVM, which is part of the EL system boundary. They are not external entities; they are internal callers.
Internal EVM component. A zkSNARK verifier contract runs within the EVM and is part of the EL, not an external entity.
Internal EVM component. Same as EXT-CALLER-CONTRACT - a contract invoking ECMUL is internal to EL.
Internal EVM component. A smart contract verifying EIP-712 signatures operates within the EVM execution environment.

Light clients read committed state (merkle roots) from the beacon chain. In the context of EIP-7928, the light client verifies access list inclusion but does not send data into the system. It is a consumer, not an input source.

Wallet software is an off-chain application that interacts with users. It does not directly send data across the EL/CL system boundary; it constructs signing requests locally. The actual trust boundary crossing occurs when the signed transaction is submitted via JSON-RPC.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer via Engine API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: The CL communicates with the EL via Engine API authenticated with JWT. The channel is authenticated but payload content (execution payloads including block access lists from EIP-7928) must be fully validated by the EL. A compromised or buggy CL could send invalid payloads.

trusted_external_entities.name: Block Proposer via P2P Gossip
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: P2P gossip (beacon block proposals containing execution payloads with block_access_list)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Block proposers are validators on the P2P network. Any validator can propose blocks, and proposals arrive over unauthenticated gossip. All block contents must be validated including EIP-7928 access list data.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer via Light Client Gossip
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any peer on the P2P network can publish light client updates via gossip. Messages are unauthenticated at the transport layer. Fork digest validation and SSZ deserialization are the first lines of defense, followed by cryptographic verification of sync committee signatures.

trusted_external_entities.name: P2P Peer via Light Client Req/Resp
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peers responding to req/resp requests are untrusted. They may provide stale, incomplete, or malicious bootstrap data or updates. Cryptographic verification of sync committee signatures is required.

trusted_external_entities.name: Prospective Validator via Deposit Contract
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Deposit contract transaction (eth_sendRawTransaction containing deposit call)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Any user can submit a deposit transaction. The deposit contract validates the transaction on-chain, but the consensus layer must validate the resulting deposit data (pubkey, withdrawal credentials, amount, signature) when processing deposits from the Merkle tree.

trusted_external_entities.name: Beacon Peer via Deposit Snapshot API
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Peers providing deposit tree snapshots for weak subjectivity sync are untrusted. The snapshot must be validated by recalculating the deposit root from finalized hashes and comparing against the transmitted deposit_root. A malicious peer could provide a fraudulent snapshot.

trusted_external_entities.name: Consensus Layer via Withdrawal Requests
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Engine API (withdrawals field in execution payload)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Validator withdrawals originate from the CL and are delivered to the EL via the authenticated Engine API. The channel is JWT-authenticated but the EL must validate withdrawal fields (index, validator_index, address, amount) to prevent creating ETH out of thin air.

trusted_external_entities.name: Network Peer via P2P Block Propagation
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Block headers received from P2P peers are completely untrusted. Full header validation is required including parent hash, state root, transactions root, receipt root, withdrawals root, blob gas fields, and parent beacon block root.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Validator Operator (Testnet)
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: Deposit contract and P2P validator registration
trusted_external_entities.rationale: In the EIP-6916 testnet reset context, any actor can deposit validators to attempt a 66% majority takeover. The reset mechanism is the primary defense. This entity is explicitly modeled as an attacker.

trusted_external_entities.name: DApp via EIP-712 Signing Request
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: eth_signTypedData_v4 JSON-RPC (EIP-712 messages with box types)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: DApps construct EIP-712 signing requests including boxed values. These are untrusted inputs that wallets must validate (box structure, inner type definitions, type isolation). Malicious DApps could craft requests to confuse users about what they are signing.

trusted_external_entities.name: User via JSON-RPC
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Archetypal EL attack vector. Any user can submit transactions via JSON-RPC. All transaction data is potentially malicious and requires full validation.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Peer via devp2p
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Archetypal EL attack vector. Malicious peers can attempt eclipse attacks, send invalid blocks or transactions. All P2P data is untrusted.

trusted_external_entities.name: Malicious Validator via CL P2P
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Archetypal CL attack vector. Malicious validators can propose invalid blocks, submit conflicting attestations, or attempt censorship. All validator messages require cryptographic verification.

trusted_external_entities.name: Checkpoint Sync Endpoint
trusted_external_entities.entry_point: HTTP checkpoint sync API (genesis state for EIP-6916 testnet resets)
trusted_external_entities.rationale: Archetypal CL attack vector for external services. Checkpoint sync endpoints could provide incorrect genesis data. In EIP-6916 context, compromised endpoints could initialize nodes with attacker-controlled validator sets.

boundary_edges.security_assumption: EL must fully validate execution payload content including block_access_list size, RLP encoding, and all header fields. JWT authentication ensures channel integrity but does not guarantee payload correctness.
EL must validate all withdrawal fields (U64 index, U64 validator_index, Address, U256 amount). Must not credit arbitrary amounts. JWT-authenticated channel but content validation required.
Must validate fork digest before SSZ deserialization. Must cryptographically verify sync committee signatures. Must reject malformed messages and apply peer scoring penalties.
Must validate fork version, SSZ deserialization, and cryptographic proofs on all responses. At least one honest peer must be available for security guarantees.
Deposit contract validates on-chain. CL must validate deposit data from Merkle tree including pubkey, withdrawal credentials, amount, and BLS signature before processing.
Must recalculate deposit root from finalized hashes and compare to transmitted deposit_root. Must verify against weak subjectivity checkpoint. Invalid snapshots must be rejected.

Full block header validation required: parent_hash, ommers_hash (empty), state_root, transactions_root, receipt_root, withdrawals_root, blob_gas_used, excess_blob_gas, parent_beacon_block_root. Invalid headers must be rejected.

boundary_edges.target_component_interface: Deposit contract and validator activation queue
boundary_edges.security_assumption: Testnet reset period must be shorter than validator takeover timeline. For 10k genesis validators, reset period must be < 5.7 days. EIP-6916 reset mechanism provides the defense.

Must validate box structure (value, primaryType, types properties present). Must validate inner type definitions follow EIP-712 rules. Must enforce type isolation (inner types cannot reference outer types). Must render box contents to user for informed consent.
Full transaction validation required: signature verification, nonce check, gas limit validation, value bounds, calldata parsing. No authentication required for public RPC endpoints.
All blocks and transactions received from peers must be fully validated. Eclipse attack mitigation required (diverse peer connections). Invalid data must result in peer scoring penalties.

All validator messages must be cryptographically verified (BLS signatures). Conflicting attestations must trigger slashing conditions. Censorship resistance depends on sufficient honest validator participation.

Checkpoint data must be verified against known weak subjectivity checkpoint. In EIP-6916, genesis_0 parameters must be hardcoded and correct. Compromised endpoints could provide fraudulent genesis state.
